A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GeN research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison across the formatting changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic optimization experiments and vision, language, generation, and recommendation results, including Tables 2–5 and 7 and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds quadratic-fit diagnostics across training in Figure 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds R² > 0.99 as a condition for updating the learning rate. New Appendix C.7 documents a variant multiplying GeN's learning rate by (1 − t/T), with cosine decay also suggested. The underlying GeN update and Algorithm 2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The synthetic functions, image datasets, E2E, GLUE, Penn-Fudan, CelebA, MovieLens-1m, and pretraining coverage are retained. Appendix D.5's additional application areas are prospective, without new evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the synthetic experiments, benchmark tables, and appendix comparisons, including Prodigy, D-adaptation, and the heuristic schedulers. Changes to BFGS citations in Table 1 do not change evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 2 extends fit validation from epoch-1 and epoch-5 snapshots to R² trajectories spanning five epochs, expanding the diagnostic's temporal sampling. Existing benchmark budgets, metrics, and preprocessing remain unchanged. Appendix C.7 newly discloses decay used for existing results without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds two trajectories assessing whether the quadratic approximation remains accurate throughout training, extending the selected-checkpoint analysis. Existing batch-size, update-frequency, initialization, model-size, and pretraining analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same uncertainty reporting, and neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional R² curves extend an existing fit diagnostic rather than introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 2 adds R² trajectories showing generally high fit quality with occasional dips. Existing benchmark values in Tables 2–5 and 7 and the original plotted results are unchanged; for example, GeN's E2E BLEU remains 67.30.

T1.justification: The generalized-inverse definition, Propositions 3.3 and 3.6, Appendix A derivations, and Appendix E's Theorem 1 and proof are retained. Equation C.1 specifies a procedural decay variant without adding a theoretical guarantee or revising the proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the claims of broadly applicable, automatic, Hessian-informed learning-rate selection with low amortized overhead and competitive performance. The conclusion broadens future directions without changing the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C.7 qualifies the T-independent formulation by suggesting that explicit decay can help when the training budget is small. Section 4 now invokes CPU off-loading in its memory-cost explanation, and Appendix D.5 expands prospective applicability to privacy, multitask optimization, and other settings.

D1.justification: v3 adds the AutoGeN repository address, discloses CPU off-loading, and states that Places365, INat2021, and NLU experiments used the decay variant in Appendix C.7. These improve implementation documentation without demonstrating that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds Liu and Bu's differential-privacy work and Jin et al.'s multitask/unlearning work. Fletcher and Shanno references are removed from the BFGS attribution. The substantive comparisons with LQA, QLABGrad, and ADLER remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording clarifications, adds short subsections C.7 and D.5, renames C.6 to emphasize preliminary results, and updates author/conference information and citation style. The main narrative and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 expands from four panels to six. Table 1 becomes taller with stacked author-year citations, Figure 15 is reduced, and floats shift under the ICLR template. The single-column organization and remaining figure content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility through code-access information, CPU off-loading disclosure, and identification of the decay variant used for existing results. Figure 2 also provides broader evidence about approximation quality across training. These are useful, limited gains: benchmark results and theory remain unchanged, and the added fit condition and decay variant are not separately ablated.
